name: Chicken
description: The default meat of all four cuisines.

unani.note: Murgh is garam — chicken soup for cold days.

histamine.note: Fresh/freshly-frozen is safe; leftovers and slow-cooked broths accumulate histamine fast.

nutrition.highlight: lean unless you eat the skin

name: Beef
description: Red meat staple, curries to burgers.

tcm.note: Neutral-to-warm; strengthening.

histamine.note: Freshness rules: freshly cooked fine; aged steak and ground beef sitting around are worse.

name: Lamb / mutton
description: The festival meat — and every tradition's warmest.

tcm.note: Yang rou is TCM's defining warming meat — winter hot pot.

unani.note: Classic garam — nihari and paya weather.

histamine.note: Fresh lamb is well tolerated; same freshness caveat as all meat.

name: Goat meat
description: Lean red meat of desi 'mutton' curries.

ayurveda.note: Notably gentler than lamb in classical texts.

histamine.note: Fresh is fine.

name: Pork
description: The staple meat of Chinese and Western kitchens.

tcm.note: Unusually for meat, TCM calls pork neutral-cool and yin-nourishing.

histamine.note: Fresh is moderate; cured forms (bacon, ham, sausage) are a 3.

nutrition.highlight: more thiamine than any other meat

name: Duck
description: Rich dark poultry; Peking duck to salan.

tcm.note: The yin poultry — opposite of chicken.

histamine.note: Fresh fine; roasted-hung preparations age the meat.

name: Egg (chicken)
description: The universal breakfast protein.

unani.note: Anda is classically garam — half-boiled eggs for winter.

histamine.note: Raw/runny egg WHITE is the liberator; well-cooked eggs are fine for most.

nutrition.highlight: the protein standard everything else is measured against

name: White fish (fresh)
description: Mild white-fleshed fish, fried or curried.

tcm.note: Most freshwater fish neutral-warm.

ayurveda.note: Fish is classically ushna — the fish+milk incompatibility rule.

unani.note: Machli is garam — a winter food in desi logic.

histamine.note: THE safe protein — but only very fresh or frozen-at-sea; histamine forms within hours unrefrigerated.

name: Salmon
description: Rich pink oily fish.

histamine.note: Fresh/frozen fine for many; SMOKED salmon is a 3.

nutrition.highlight: omega-3, and the fat is the point

name: Tuna (canned)
description: Pantry protein — and the textbook histamine hazard.

tcm.note: Thinly classified.

histamine.note: Scombroid fish: histamine forms before canning — the classic 'fish poisoning' is a histamine event.

nutrition.highlight: cheap protein, and the textbook histamine hazard

name: Sardines (canned)
description: Small oily canned fish.

histamine.note: Scombroid-class; canned small oily fish run very high.

name: Mackerel
description: Strong-flavored oily fish.

histamine.note: The namesake scombroid fish — spoils into histamine fastest of all.

nutrition.highlight: oilier than salmon, and spoils faster

name: Shrimp / prawns
description: Sweet shellfish of every coast.

tcm.note: A yang-tonifying food in TCM.

unani.note: Jhinga is famously garam in desi usage.

histamine.note: Shellfish are liberators; freshness critical.

nutrition.highlight: cooks in ninety seconds and toughens in two minutes

name: Crab
description: Sweet shellfish — famously 'cold' in Chinese food culture.

tcm.note: So cold it's traditionally eaten with warming ginger vinegar.

ayurveda.note: Shellfish heating per most; disagrees with TCM.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator; eat very fresh.

name: Squid
description: Chewy cephalopod, grilled or fried.

histamine.note: Moderate; freshness critical as with all seafood.

nutrition.highlight: thirty seconds or thirty minutes — nothing between

name: Tofu
description: Fresh soybean curd.

histamine.note: Fresh tofu is moderate; fermented tofu (furu) and aged forms are a 3.

name: Edamame
description: Young green soybeans in the pod.

histamine.note: Milder than mature soy.

nutrition.highlight: a complete protein you eat with your fingers

name: Chickpeas
description: The legume of chole, hummus, and besan.

ayurveda.note: Cooling-dry per texts — yet desi folk calls chana garam; both recorded.

unani.note: Nakhud is garam in Unani sources.

histamine.note: Legumes are mildly flagged; usually fine fresh-cooked.

name: Red lentils (masoor)
description: Fast-cooking everyday dal; shorbat adas.

tcm.note: Lentils thinly classified in TCM.

ayurveda.note: Masoor is one of the warmer dals.

histamine.note: Fresh-cooked dal is fine for most; reheated day-old less so.

nutrition.highlight: collapse to purée in twenty minutes

name: Brown/green lentils
description: Whole lentils of mujadara and soups.

histamine.note: As legumes generally.

nutrition.highlight: hold their shape where red lentils dissolve

name: Mung beans
description: The gentlest dal — and TCM's classic heat-clearing bean.

tcm.note: Lu dou soup is THE TCM summer cooler and detoxifier.

ayurveda.note: The sattvic, tridoshic dal of khichdi.

histamine.note: Among the safest legumes fresh-cooked.

nutrition.highlight: the gentlest dal on a bad stomach

name: Urad dal (black gram)
description: Heavy creamy dal of dal makhani and dosa batter.

tcm.note: Thinly classified.

ayurveda.note: The heaviest, most heating dal — a strength-builder.

histamine.note: Fermented forms (dosa/idli batter) add histamine.

nutrition.highlight: creamy enough to need no cream

name: Kidney beans (rajma)
description: Red beans of rajma-chawal and chili.

histamine.note: As legumes; canned versions slightly worse than home-cooked.

nutrition.highlight: must be boiled hard — undercooked is worse than raw

name: Black beans
description: Earthy beans; TCM's kidney-nourishing hei dou.

tcm.note: Black color = kidney-tonifying, gently warming.

histamine.note: Fermented black beans (douchi) are a 3 — different food.

name: Black-eyed peas (lobia)
description: Quick-cooking spotted beans.

ayurveda.note: Lighter than most beans; schools vary.

histamine.note: As legumes.

name: Fava beans (ful)
description: The bean of Egypt's national breakfast.

unani.note: Baqilla leans cold-heavy in Unani texts — hence the warming cumin/oil dressing.

histamine.note: Histamine-modest — but causes favism in G6PD-deficient people (a separate, serious issue).

name: Soybeans
description: The mother bean of tofu, soy milk, and sauce.

histamine.note: Higher than other legumes; fermented soy products higher still.

nutrition.highlight: the only common bean with all nine amino acids

name: Peanuts
description: The everyday roasted legume-nut.

unani.note: Moongphali is winter street food — classic garam.

histamine.note: Liberator — and a major true allergen besides.

nutrition.highlight: a legume that everyone files under nuts

name: Almonds
description: The prized nut of badam milk and Unani tonics.

ayurveda.note: Heating — but soaked & peeled becomes neutral-building, per classical rule.

unani.note: Badam is garam; sardai (soaked-ground) tempers it.

histamine.note: Among the better-tolerated nuts.

nutrition.highlight: vitamin E, and soaked overnight in half of Asia

name: Walnuts
description: Brain-shaped nut; TCM's kidney-warming tonic.

tcm.note: A classic yang/kidney tonic.

unani.note: Akhrot is textbook garam — winter food.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 3 — the highest-rated nut, and well above the others.

nutrition.highlight: the only common nut with plant omega-3

name: Cashews
description: Creamy nut of korma pastes and snack tins.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 1 — well below walnuts, which it is often lumped in with.

nutrition.highlight: never sold raw — the shell is caustic

name: Pistachios
description: Green nut of kheer, kunafa, and baklava.

unani.note: Pista is garam in Unani texts.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 0 — one of the safest nuts, not a middling one.

nutrition.highlight: the green is lutein, not dye

name: Pine nuts
description: Delicate nut of fatteh, pesto, and chilgoza winters.

unani.note: Chilgoza/snobar is a classic winter garam nut.

histamine.note: Usually fine; rancidity is the bigger issue.

nutrition.highlight: delicate oils that go rancid within weeks

name: Pumpkin seeds
description: Green flat seeds, roasted for snacking.

unani.note: Seed used in cooling majoons by some hakims.

histamine.note: A histamine-safe snack seed.

name: Sunflower seeds
description: The cracking-snack seed of Chinese and Arab gatherings.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 2, higher than most seeds; rancid ones are worse again.

nutrition.highlight: vitamin E, eaten by the handful across two continents

name: Chia seeds
description: Gel-forming little seeds (often confused with desi sabja — see basil seeds).

tcm.note: New-world; not classical.

ayurveda.note: Used like cooling sabja in modern practice; not classical.

unani.note: Treated like tukh malanga in modern desi use.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Flaxseed
description: Oily seed ground into winter pinnis and porridges.

ayurveda.note: Alsi is classically ushna — a winter laddu seed.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Chana dal
description: Split husked bengal gram — holds its shape, so it never turns to mush.

tcm.note: Follows the chickpea; no strong Chinese classification.

ayurveda.note: Chanaka is shita and ruksha — cooling but drying and wind-forming.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk, which is why it is cooked with hing and ginger.

histamine.note: Low cooked. Legumes are the classic wind problem, not a histamine one.

name: Toor dal
description: The everyday yellow dal — the base of sambar and of dal fry.

tcm.note: No classical Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Adhaki is shita and kashaya, and lighter than the heavier dals.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk; tempered with hot spices for exactly that reason.

histamine.note: Low cooked fresh; dal kept warm overnight is a different matter.

name: Kala chana
description: Small dark chickpeas, soaked overnight and boiled whole.

tcm.note: Read with the chickpea.

ayurveda.note: Chanaka is shita, though the whole black kind is heavier than the split.

unani.note: Desi usage separates the two: kala chana is treated as garam where safed chana is not.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Moth beans
description: Tiny brown beans, usually sprouted — the base of misal.

tcm.note: No Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and laghu — light but warming, unlike most of the cooling dals.

unani.note: Garam and drying in regional usage.

histamine.note: Low. Sprouting is a food-safety question, not a histamine one.

name: Horse gram
description: Hard, dark, strongly flavoured pulse — the most heating thing in the dal drawer.

tcm.note: Outside the Chinese record; placed from its drying, dispersing character.

ayurveda.note: Kulattha is ushna and tikshna in a high degree — the classical drug for stones and for excess kapha and fat.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; given to break stones and dry damp conditions.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Pinto beans
description: Speckled beans that cook down creamy — refried, or stewed whole.

tcm.note: A new-world bean; read with the legume family.

ayurveda.note: Grouped with the heavier beans, which are ushna and vata-provoking.

histamine.note: Low cooked; tinned beans sit in brine, which is a separate matter.

name: Lima beans
description: Large flat pale beans with a buttery, floury texture.

tcm.note: Read with the bean family.

ayurveda.note: Heavy and read as shita; no classical entry.

histamine.note: Low cooked. Raw or undercooked lima beans are toxic — a cyanide question, not histamine.

name: Turkey
description: Lean poultry, mostly roasted whole — and eaten as leftovers for days.

tcm.note: Read with chicken, which is warm and qi-tonifying.

unani.note: Garam, leaner and drier than chicken.

histamine.note: Low fresh — but turkey is the classic leftover meat, and cooked meat climbs sharply after a day or two in the fridge.

name: Quail
description: Small game bird, roasted or curried whole — two to a person.

tcm.note: An chun tonifies qi and strengthens the tendons and bones.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; game birds are the heating end of the meat group.

unani.note: Bater is famously garam in desi Unani usage, given in winter and for weakness.

histamine.note: Low fresh, like other poultry.

name: Liver
description: Iron-dense organ meat — fried hard with onions, or grilled on skewers.

tcm.note: Liver tonifies liver blood in the Chinese reading — like treats like, and it is given for blood deficiency.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree; organ meats are the most heating of the mamsa group.

unani.note: Kaleji is textbook garam-khushk — winter food, and held back in summer.

histamine.note: Organ meats are among the highest — they spoil fastest, and histamine forms before anything smells wrong.

name: Kidney
description: Firm organ meat with a mineral edge — soaked before cooking to soften it.

tcm.note: Kidney tonifies the kidney and warms yang in the Chinese reading — a classic winter dish.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, with the other organ meats.

unani.note: Gurda is garam-khushk and strengthening in the Unani record.

histamine.note: High, like all offal.

nutrition.highlight: soaked and rinsed, or it tastes of ammonia

name: Bone broth
description: Bones simmered for hours until the stock turns to jelly when cold.

tcm.note: Long-simmered bone soups are the archetypal warming tonic — gu tang builds qi, blood and marrow.

ayurveda.note: Mamsa rasa is ushna and building — given in convalescence.

unani.note: Yakhni is garam-tar, the standard Unani food for weakness and recovery.

histamine.note: The hours of simmering that make it nourishing are exactly what builds histamine — the reason a 'healing' broth flares some people badly.

name: Salami
description: Pork cured, fermented and air-dried for weeks — sliced thin, eaten cold.

tcm.note: Salted, cured and dried; read as hot and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — preserved meat sits outside the classical texts.

unani.note: Garam-khushk by its salt and its curing.

histamine.note: Fermented and aged meat — one of the highest-histamine foods on the SIGHI list, and the reason a cold-cut sandwich flares people.

name: Bacon
description: Pork belly cured in salt and usually smoked, then fried crisp.

tcm.note: Pork itself is neutral-cool; curing, salting and smoking turn it hot and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru; outside the classical record.

histamine.note: Cured and smoked — high, and worth knowing about before a breakfast blamed on the eggs.

name: Cod
description: Firm white flakes with almost no oil — the fish-and-chips fish.

tcm.note: Read with the white fish, which are neutral and easily digested.

ayurveda.note: Matsya is classed as ushna in Ayurveda, whatever the fish.

histamine.note: Low if genuinely fresh or frozen at sea. Every fish climbs fast once it thaws and sits.

name: Tilapia
description: Mild farmed white fish, cheap and everywhere.

tcm.note: With the white fish — neutral and gentle.

histamine.note: Low fresh; the usual fish caveat about time and temperature applies.

name: Pomfret
description: Flat silver sea fish, shallow-fried whole with a chilli rub.

tcm.note: Read with the white sea fish.

unani.note: Garam-tar; fish is warming in the Unani record, and famously not eaten with milk.

histamine.note: Low fresh off the boat, which is how it is usually bought.

name: Rohu
description: The everyday river carp of Bengal and Punjab — bony, and worth it.

tcm.note: Carp is warm in TCM and used to drain damp and swelling.

ayurveda.note: Freshwater matsya is explicitly ushna — the most heating of the fish group.

unani.note: Garam-tar; river fish is treated as warmer than sea fish.

histamine.note: Low when fresh — river fish is usually sold live or same-day for this reason.

name: Hilsa
description: The oily monsoon river fish Bengal builds a season around.

tcm.note: Oily river fish; read with carp.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and snigdha — oily and heating, in the freshwater group.

unani.note: Garam-tar in a high degree, for its oil.

histamine.note: Oily fish spoils faster than lean; hilsa is often salted or smoked, which pushes it higher again.

name: Anchovies
description: Tiny fish packed in salt or oil, melting into whatever they're cooked in.

tcm.note: Salted and oily; read with the small oily fish.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, more so for the salt.

histamine.note: Salted and matured small fish — the same family as the tinned tuna and sardines already flagged, and usually worse.

name: Mussels
description: Steamed open in their black shells — sweet, briny, quick.

tcm.note: Shellfish are warming and yang-tonifying in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; shellfish is the heating end of the group.

unani.note: Garam; treated as strengthening and aphrodisiac.

histamine.note: Shellfish are liberators — the flag on shrimp applies here too, and they must be alive when cooked.

name: Clams
description: Small hinged shells, cooked just until they open.

tcm.note: Unusually for shellfish, clams are cold in TCM and used to clear heat and phlegm.

unani.note: Garam in the general reading of shellfish.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator.

name: Oysters
description: Eaten raw off the shell, or dried and simmered into stock.

tcm.note: Mu li is cool and yin-nourishing — the shell is a classical calming drug.

ayurveda.note: Ushna with the shellfish; outside classical practice.

histamine.note: Raw shellfish is both a liberator and high in itself — among the riskiest things on a reactive day.

name: Scallops
description: Sweet white discs seared hard and fast; dried, they become a prized stock base.

tcm.note: Gan bei is neutral and nourishes yin — the dried scallop is a tonic ingredient.

unani.note: Garam by the general shellfish reading.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator; the dried kind is higher again.

name: Tempeh
description: Whole soybeans bound into a firm cake by an edible mould.

tcm.note: Read with soy; the ferment adds a warming quality.

ayurveda.note: Fermented, so ushna — unlike plain tofu, which is shita.

unani.note: Garam by its ferment; outside the classical record.

histamine.note: A deliberate mould ferment — high, and a common surprise for people who switched to it from tofu.

name: Seitan
description: Wheat dough washed until only the gluten is left — chewy and meat-like.

tcm.note: Mian jin follows wheat, which is cool.

ayurveda.note: Read with wheat; very guru and hard to digest.

histamine.note: Low in itself; the marinades and sauces it comes in usually are not.

name: Soy chunks
description: Defatted soy flour extruded into spongy nuggets — soaked, squeezed, curried.

tcm.note: Read with soy; a modern processed form with no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Follows the soybean, which is shita and guru.

histamine.note: Low — unfermented, unlike soy sauce, miso and tempeh.

name: Lupini beans
description: Brined yellow beans sold as street snacks — bitter unless soaked for days.

tcm.note: No Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Bitter and drying; read as ushna.

unani.note: Turmus is garam-khushk in the Arab record, taken as a bitter tonic.

histamine.note: Sold in brine after a long soak — the brining is what lifts it.

name: Peanut butter
description: Roasted peanuts ground to a paste, sometimes with sugar and palm oil.

tcm.note: Follows the peanut; roasting and grinding concentrate it.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — heavier again than whole peanuts.

histamine.note: Carries the peanut's liberator flag; long storage after opening adds to it.

name: Hazelnuts
description: Round sweet nuts, best after roasting rubs the skins off.

tcm.note: Zhen zi is neutral and tonifies the spleen and stomach.

ayurveda.note: Ushna with the nut group; no separate classical entry.

unani.note: Bunduq is garam-tar in the Unani record, strengthening to the brain.

histamine.note: Lower than walnuts, which SIGHI flags as a liberator.

nutrition.highlight: roast, then rub the skins off

name: Macadamia nuts
description: Buttery white nuts with the highest fat of any — and a shell that fights back.

tcm.note: No classical entry; read with the nut group.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru, for its oil.

unani.note: Garam-tar by the general rule for oily nuts.

histamine.note: Low; one of the better-tolerated nuts.

name: Pecans
description: Long ridged nuts, sweeter and softer than walnuts.

tcm.note: Read with walnut, which is warm and tonifies the kidney.

histamine.note: Lower than walnut, though the two are close relatives. They go rancid quickly.

name: Brazil nuts
description: Large dense nuts — one or two a day is the whole selenium requirement.

tcm.note: No classical entry; read with the oily nuts.

unani.note: Garam-tar by the general nut reading.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 0. Selenium toxicity from eating many is a real and separate caution.

nutrition.highlight: one or two is a full day's selenium

name: Hemp seeds
description: Soft green-white kernels with a mild nutty taste, scattered raw.

tcm.note: Huo ma ren is neutral and moistening — a classical gentle laxative for dry constipation.

ayurveda.note: Read with the oily seeds; the classical entries concern the plant, not the food seed.

unani.note: Garam-tar by the general seed reading.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 0.

name: Watermelon seeds
description: Hulled white kernels — ground into thickeners, or cracked as a snack.

tcm.note: Follows the melon, which is cold; the seed is milder.

ayurveda.note: Shita, with the melon-seed group — a summer thickener.

unani.note: Magaz is thanda-tar and one of the classic Unani cooling seeds.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Four-seed mix
description: Melon, cucumber, pumpkin and watermelon kernels together — the thandai thickener.

tcm.note: Read from its components, all of them cooling seeds.

ayurveda.note: Every one of the four is shita; the blend exists specifically to cool.

unani.note: Char magaz is a named Unani cooling compound, used in thandai and in brain tonics.

histamine.note: Low; they go rancid quickly once ground.

name: Adzuki beans
description: Small red beans boiled into sweet paste, or simmered as a damp-draining soup.

tcm.note: Chi xiao dou is neutral and drains damp — the classical bean for swelling and water retention.

ayurveda.note: Shita and light; a cooling pulse.

unani.note: Thanda; outside the classical Unani record.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Split peas
description: Dried peas split and hulled — they collapse into soup rather than holding shape.

tcm.note: Read with peas, which are neutral and spleen-strengthening.

ayurveda.note: Shita and ruksha, like the other cooling pulses.

histamine.note: Low cooked.

name: Whole moong
description: Mung beans with the skin on — sprouted, or cooked into a heavier dal than the split kind.

tcm.note: Lv dou is cold and the classical summer heat-clearing bean.

ayurveda.note: Mudga is shita and the lightest of the pulses — named in the texts as suitable in illness.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk; moong ki dal is what the sick are fed.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Soybean sprouts
description: Sprouted soybeans with the yellow head still attached — firmer than mung sprouts.

tcm.note: Read with the sprouts, which clear heat and drain damp.

ayurveda.note: Shita; sprouting lightens the heavy soybean.

histamine.note: Low fresh; sprouts spoil quickly, which is a food-safety matter.

name: Natto
description: Soybeans fermented with bacillus until they string — pungent, sticky and divisive.

tcm.note: Read with the fermented soy group; warming.

ayurveda.note: Fermented, so ushna, unlike plain soy.

unani.note: Garam by ferment; outside the classical record.

histamine.note: One of the highest-histamine foods there is — a deliberate bacterial ferment eaten without cooking.

name: Tofu skin
description: The film lifted off simmering soy milk and dried — chewy once rehydrated.

tcm.note: Read with tofu, which is cool and moistening.

histamine.note: Low — unfermented, unlike the soy sauces and pastes.

name: Fermented tofu
description: Tofu cubes aged in brine and rice wine into a salty, cheese-like paste.

tcm.note: Fermented and salted; warming.

histamine.note: Months of brine fermentation, often with rice wine — high, and used in small salty amounts.

name: Duck egg
description: Larger and richer than a hen's egg, with a deeper yolk.

tcm.note: Ya dan is cool and yin-nourishing in TCM, unlike the neutral hen's egg.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna; the duck egg is richer again.

unani.note: Garam-tar in a higher degree than a hen's egg.

histamine.note: Egg is a liberator on the SIGHI list; the duck egg is no different.

name: Quail egg
description: Tiny speckled eggs, boiled whole and eaten several at a time.

tcm.note: An chun dan is neutral and tonifying, milder than the bird itself.

histamine.note: Egg liberator flag applies.

name: Century egg
description: Duck eggs cured in alkaline clay for months until the white turns to dark jelly.

tcm.note: Read with duck egg; the alkaline cure is cooling and descending.

ayurveda.note: Ushna as an egg; the preservation has no classical parallel.

histamine.note: Months of alkaline curing on an egg base — both the egg's liberator flag and a heavy preserved-protein load.

name: Mutton
description: Meat from a grown sheep — stronger, fattier and slower-cooking than lamb.

tcm.note: Yang rou is one of the warmest meats in TCM, given through winter to warm yang.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru in a high degree.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; classic winter and celebration meat.

histamine.note: Low fresh; like all red meat it climbs once cut and stored.

name: Camel meat
description: Lean dark meat from the Gulf and the Sahel, cooked long and slow.

tcm.note: Absent from the Chinese record; read with the red meats.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru, in the mamsa group.

unani.note: Garam-khushk in the Arab and Unani record — a strengthening winter meat.

histamine.note: Low fresh.

name: Ham
description: Pork leg cured in salt, sometimes smoked, sliced thin and eaten cold.

tcm.note: Cured and salted; hot and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru; preserved meat is outside the classical texts.

histamine.note: Cured meat, like salami and bacon — one of the highest-histamine categories on the SIGHI list.

name: Sausage
description: Minced meat and fat in a casing — fresh, cured or smoked depending on where you are.

tcm.note: Minced fatty meat, usually fried.

histamine.note: Minced, seasoned and usually cured or fermented — high whichever style it is.

name: Dried fish
description: Fish salted and sun-dried for months — pounded into curries and sambals.

tcm.note: Salted and dried; warming and drying.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree — matsya, salted and concentrated.

histamine.note: Salted, dried and aged fish is the single highest-histamine food category there is — well above tinned tuna.

name: Fish roe
description: Salted fish eggs — served in small spoonfuls, and intensely savoury.

tcm.note: Read with fish; salted and concentrated.

histamine.note: Salted and cured fish product — high, and eaten cold without cooking.

name: Surimi
description: White fish minced to paste, bound with starch and shaped — the crab stick.

tcm.note: Read with white fish; heavily processed.

histamine.note: The fish is processed and stored a long time before it reaches you, which is what lifts it.

name: Prawns
description: Larger than shrimp and sold under a dozen names — grilled, curried, or fried in batter.

tcm.note: Xia is warm and yang-tonifying in TCM, and reputed as an aphrodisiac.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree; shellfish is the heating end of the group.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; famously not eaten with milk in desi practice.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator, like shrimp — and they spoil fast.

name: Lobster
description: Large clawed shellfish, boiled or grilled and eaten from the shell.

tcm.note: Read with the shellfish group — warm and yang-tonifying.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator; must be cooked from live for the same reason.

name: Octopus
description: Firm, mild and rubbery unless cooked either very fast or very slow.

tcm.note: Read with the cephalopods; neutral and nourishing.

histamine.note: Seafood liberator flag.

name: Apricot kernel
description: The almond-like seed inside the apricot stone — bitter, and used in small amounts.

tcm.note: Xing ren is warm, descends lung qi and stops cough — one of the standard cough drugs.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and snigdha; used for the chest.

histamine.note: Low. Bitter kernels contain amygdalin and are eaten in small quantity for that reason — a toxicity matter, not histamine.

name: Chironji
description: Small lens-shaped seeds used like almonds in kheer and mithai.

tcm.note: No classical Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and snigdha; grouped with the nuts in Ayurvedic sweets.

histamine.note: Low; they go rancid quickly.

name: Lotus nut
description: The fresh green seed eaten raw from the pod, before it is dried.

tcm.note: Lian zi is neutral and calms the shen; the green plumule inside is bitter and cold.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Whey protein
description: Milk protein isolated and dried — the gym powder.

tcm.note: A modern isolate; read with dairy.

ayurveda.note: Follows milk; no classical entry for the isolate.

histamine.note: Processed dairy that sits on shelves for months; flavoured versions add more.

name: Sprouted chana
description: Chickpeas soaked and sprouted, eaten raw with lemon and onion.

tcm.note: Read with chickpea; sprouting lightens it.

ayurveda.note: Shita and lighter than the cooked bean.

histamine.note: Low, though raw sprouts are a food-safety question of their own.

name: Goose
description: Dark rich poultry with far more fat than duck — roasted whole.

tcm.note: E rou is neutral to warm and tonifies qi in the Chinese reading.

histamine.note: Low fresh.

name: Rabbit
description: Very lean pale meat that dries out unless cooked in liquid.

tcm.note: Tu rou is cool in TCM — unusual among meats, and given in heat conditions.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, but among the lighter meats.

histamine.note: Low fresh.

name: Venison
description: Very lean dark game meat with a strong flavour.

tcm.note: Lu rou is warm and strongly yang-tonifying — a winter tonic meat in TCM.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree, as game is.

histamine.note: Low fresh, though game is often hung, which raises it considerably.

name: Tripe
description: Stomach lining, cleaned and simmered for hours until tender.

tcm.note: Read with the offal group; warming and tonifying to the stomach.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, with the other organ meats.

histamine.note: Offal, and then simmered for hours — both mechanisms at once.

name: Trotters
description: Feet simmered overnight until the collagen turns the broth to jelly.

tcm.note: Collagen-rich slow-cooked meat is warming and strongly tonifying in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — a building food.

unani.note: Garam-tar; the classic winter and postpartum strengthener.

histamine.note: The overnight simmer that makes paya what it is builds histamine the whole time — the same trap as bone broth.

name: Brisket
description: A tough chest cut that only works cooked long and low.

tcm.note: Read with beef; slow cooking warms further.

histamine.note: Fresh beef is low; the hours of cooking raise it, and it is usually made ahead.

name: Oxtail
description: Gelatinous tail joints braised until the meat slides off.

tcm.note: Collagen-rich slow-cooked meat is warming and tonifying in the Chinese reading.

histamine.note: Hours of braising on a collagen-rich cut — the bone-broth problem again.

name: Marrow bone
description: The fatty marrow inside a shin bone, roasted or dropped into nihari.

tcm.note: Marrow is a classical yin-and-essence tonic in TCM, warm and building.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and extremely guru — majja is the deepest tissue.

unani.note: Garam-tar; the most strengthening part of the animal in Unani usage.

histamine.note: Long-cooked bone product; the same mechanism as broth.

name: Chicken feet
description: Almost pure skin, cartilage and collagen — steamed with black bean, or simmered for stock.

tcm.note: Collagen-rich; warming and tonifying.

histamine.note: Long-cooked collagen, usually with fermented black bean on top.

name: Gizzard
description: The muscular stomach of a bird — dense, chewy and strongly flavoured.

tcm.note: Read with the offal group.

histamine.note: Offal, which spoils faster than muscle meat.

name: Brain
description: Soft rich organ meat, fried with onion and egg or curried as bheja fry.

tcm.note: Read with the offal; rich and tonifying.

unani.note: Garam-tar in a high degree; classically a brain and nerve tonic.

histamine.note: Offal, and the most perishable part of the animal.

name: Tongue
description: A dense muscle that must be boiled and peeled before it is worth eating.

tcm.note: Read with red meat.

histamine.note: Offal, and long-boiled.

name: Corned beef
description: Brisket cured in brine for days, then boiled or tinned.

tcm.note: Salt-cured; hot and damp-forming.

histamine.note: Cured meat — the same category as salami and ham.

name: Spam
description: Tinned pressed pork with salt and starch — a Pacific and Hong Kong staple.

tcm.note: Cured, salted and tinned.

histamine.note: Cured and long-stored processed meat.

name: Pâté
description: Liver blended with fat into a smooth spread, sealed under butter.

tcm.note: Read with liver.

histamine.note: Liver plus ageing under a fat seal — offal and storage together.

name: Black pudding
description: Blood, fat and grain set in a casing and sliced for frying.

tcm.note: Blood is a classical blood tonic in TCM; warming.

histamine.note: Blood-based and cured — very high.

name: Pastrami
description: Brined, spiced, smoked and steamed beef, sliced thin.

tcm.note: Cured and smoked.

histamine.note: Cured and smoked meat.

name: Jerky
description: Lean meat marinated and dried until it keeps for months.

tcm.note: Salted, dried and concentrated.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and ruksha in a high degree.

histamine.note: Dried cured meat — high, and easy to eat a lot of without noticing.

name: Biltong
description: Vinegar-cured beef air-dried in strips — drier and less sweet than jerky.

tcm.note: Cured and dried.

histamine.note: Vinegar-cured and air-dried — both raise it.

name: Smoked salmon
description: Salmon cured in salt and cold-smoked, sliced thin and eaten raw.

tcm.note: Read with salmon; curing and smoking add heat.

histamine.note: Cured, smoked and eaten without cooking — one of the highest fish preparations there is.

name: Kippers
description: Herring split, salted and cold-smoked — a traditional British breakfast.

tcm.note: Oily fish, cured and smoked.

histamine.note: Smoked oily fish — the worst combination of fish type and preparation.

name: Eel
description: Rich oily fish, usually grilled with a sweet glaze or curried in Bengal.

tcm.note: Man yu is warm and strongly tonifying in TCM — a building food.

histamine.note: Oily fish, and usually sold pre-cooked and glazed.

nutrition.highlight: rich enough to be a main

name: Sea bass
description: Firm white fish, steamed whole in Chinese kitchens and grilled in Levantine ones.

tcm.note: Lu yu is neutral and tonifies the spleen and stomach.

histamine.note: Low fresh — the usual fish caveat about time applies.

name: Snapper
description: Pink-skinned sea fish with firm sweet flesh, good whole or in fillets.

tcm.note: Read with the white sea fish.

histamine.note: Low fresh.

name: Mahi mahi
description: Dense meaty fish that grills like a steak.

tcm.note: Read with the larger sea fish.

histamine.note: A scombroid-family relative — it develops histamine fast if the cold chain slips, which is the classic fish-poisoning mechanism.

name: Catfish
description: Whiskered freshwater fish, muddy-tasting unless very fresh — long fed to convalescents.

tcm.note: A freshwater fish; warm in TCM and tonifying.

unani.note: Garam-tar; magur is given to the recovering in Bengal.

histamine.note: Low fresh; usually sold live for that reason.

name: Abalone
description: Prized shellfish, slow-braised for hours or sliced paper-thin — a banquet ingredient.

tcm.note: Bao yu nourishes yin and calms liver yang; the shell is a classical drug.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator; the dried kind is much higher.

name: Sea cucumber
description: A sea creature dried and rehydrated over days — gelatinous, and prized far beyond its flavour.

tcm.note: Hai shen is warm and tonifies kidney yang and essence — a classical tonic food.

histamine.note: Dried seafood, rehydrated over days — moderate, and higher if the soak is warm.

name: Jellyfish
description: Salt-cured and shredded, served cold in sesame dressing — texture and nothing else.

tcm.note: Hai zhe is neutral to cool and softens hardness.

histamine.note: Salt-cured for weeks before sale.

name: Almond butter
description: Roasted almonds ground to a paste — the gentler alternative to peanut butter.

tcm.note: Read with almonds.

histamine.note: Lower than peanut butter, which carries a liberator flag; almonds do not.

name: Pumpkin seed butter
description: Ground roasted pumpkin seeds — dark green, and faintly bitter.

tcm.note: Read with pumpkin seeds.

histamine.note: Low; goes rancid fast once opened.

name: Protein bar
description: Compressed protein isolate, syrup and nuts in a wrapper.

tcm.note: A modern processed food; no classical entry.

histamine.note: Whey or soy isolate with dried fruit and long shelf life.

name: Pea protein
description: Pea protein isolated and dried — the usual base of plant-based meat.

tcm.note: A modern isolate; read with peas.

histamine.note: Low; unfermented, unlike soy pastes.

name: Chicken sausage
description: Minced chicken in a casing — leaner than pork, and usually pre-cooked.

tcm.note: Read with chicken; minced and seasoned.

histamine.note: Minced, cured and pre-cooked — the processing decides it, not the bird.

name: Foie gras
description: The deliberately fattened liver of a duck or goose, served as a terrine or seared.

tcm.note: Read with liver; extremely rich.

histamine.note: Liver, aged as a terrine — offal plus storage.

nutrition.highlight: rich past the point of sense

name: Katsuobushi
description: Skipjack tuna smoked, fermented with mould and dried to a block hard as wood, then shaved.

tcm.note: Dried and smoked fish; warming and concentrating.

ayurveda.note: Matsya, dried and concentrated — firmly ushna.

histamine.note: Smoked, mould-fermented and aged for months — one of the highest-histamine ingredients in any kitchen, and it is the base of nearly every Japanese broth.

nutrition.highlight: the base of nearly every broth

name: Chikuwa
description: Fish paste moulded round a stick and grilled, leaving a hollow tube.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with the processed white fish.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with fish.

histamine.note: Processed fish paste, stored a long time before sale.

name: Kamaboko
description: Steamed fish paste in a pink-rimmed loaf, sliced thin over noodles.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with the processed white fish.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with fish.

histamine.note: Processed and long-stored fish paste.

name: Hanpen
description: Fish paste whipped with yam until it floats — soft, white and almost weightless.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with the fish pastes.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with fish.

histamine.note: Processed fish paste.

name: Satsuma age
description: Fish paste deep-fried into patties, dropped into oden.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; fried fish paste; the frying warms it.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with fried fish.

histamine.note: Processed fish, then fried.

name: Mentaiko
description: Pollock roe cured in salt and chilli — sliced over rice, or stirred through pasta.

tcm.note: Cured roe with chilli; warming.

histamine.note: Salt-cured roe — a preserved fish product, and eaten raw.

name: Ikura
description: Large salmon eggs cured in soy and sake — they burst rather than chew.

tcm.note: Cured roe; read with the fish roes.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with fish roe, treated as strengthening.

histamine.note: Soy-cured raw roe.

name: Uni
description: The gonads of a sea urchin, eaten raw — custardy, briny and divisive.

tcm.note: Shellfish of the cooling kind in the Chinese reading; yin-nourishing.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; read with the shellfish, which are ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with shellfish.

histamine.note: Raw shellfish that spoils within hours — the single most time-critical item in the set.

name: Toro
description: The fatty belly of bluefin tuna, marbled and served raw.

tcm.note: Oily fish; warming and building.

histamine.note: Tuna is a scombroid — it builds histamine faster than almost any other fish, and this is eaten raw.

name: Anago
description: Sea eel simmered soft and glazed with a sweet reduction — lighter than unagi.

tcm.note: Read with eel, which is warm and strongly tonifying in TCM.

histamine.note: Cooked and glazed; the sweet tare is a long-kept reduction.

name: Abura-age
description: Thin tofu slices fried until they puff hollow — the pouch in inari sushi.

tcm.note: Read with tofu; the frying warms it somewhat.

histamine.note: Low; unfermented soy.

name: Atsuage
description: Thick tofu blocks fried so the outside crusts and the middle stays soft.

tcm.note: Read with tofu.

histamine.note: Low; unfermented soy.

name: Fresh yuba
description: The skin lifted straight off simmering soy milk and eaten soft, not dried.

tcm.note: Read with tofu.

histamine.note: Low, though it must be eaten the day it is made.

name: Candlenut
description: Waxy nut ground to thicken curry pastes — mildly toxic raw, harmless once cooked.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; an oily nut; read with the nut group.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna and snigdha, as nuts are.

histamine.note: Low. It must be cooked — raw candlenut is a purgative, which is a separate matter.

name: Chorizo
description: Paprika-heavy pork sausage — cured and sliced in Spain, fresh and crumbled in Mexico.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; cured or fresh, both heavily spiced with paprika.

histamine.note: The Spanish kind is cured, so very high; the Mexican kind is fresh and lower — worth distinguishing.

nutrition.highlight: cured in Spain, fresh in Mexico

name: Longaniza
description: A long thin sausage, sweeter or more aniseed than chorizo depending on the country.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; spiced pork sausage.

histamine.note: Cured sausage.

name: Cecina
description: Beef salted, pressed thin and air-dried — sliced and grilled fast.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; salted and air-dried beef.

histamine.note: Air-dried cured meat.

name: Egusi seeds
description: Ground melon seeds that thicken soup and turn it grainy — the base of egusi.

tcm.note: Read with the melon seeds, which are cooling.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; the melon seeds are classical Unani coolers.

histamine.note: Low; they go rancid quickly once ground.

name: Salo
description: Slabs of pork back fat cured in salt and garlic, sliced thin and eaten cold on rye.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; salt-cured fat; read as hot and damp-forming.

histamine.note: Cured pork, eaten without cooking.

name: Kielbasa
description: Smoked garlic pork sausage, sold in a horseshoe and eaten hot or cold.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; smoked and cured pork.

histamine.note: Cured and smoked meat.

name: Kabanos
description: Long thin pork sausages dried hard — a snack rather than a meal.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; dried cured pork.

histamine.note: Air-dried cured meat.

name: Sudzhuk
description: Flat dried beef sausage heavy with garlic and cumin, sliced very thin.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; air-dried cured beef.

histamine.note: Fermented and air-dried.

name: Chinese sausage
description: Sweet dried pork sausage, hard until it is steamed on top of rice.

tcm.note: Cured, sweetened and warming.

histamine.note: Cured and air-dried pork.

name: Dried scallop
description: Scallops dried hard into amber discs and shredded into soup and congee for depth.

tcm.note: Dried shellfish; read as building.

histamine.note: Dried shellfish — one of the highest categories there is.

name: Dried squid
description: Squid dried stiff, then toasted or soaked back to life.

tcm.note: Dried seafood.

histamine.note: Dried seafood.

name: Salted duck egg
description: Duck egg cured in brine for a month — the yolk goes orange, firm and oily.

tcm.note: Duck egg is cooler than hen; the cure warms it.

histamine.note: Egg plus a month-long salt cure.

nutrition.highlight: the yolk goes orange and oily

name: Silkie chicken
description: Black-boned chicken simmered whole into tonic soup rather than eaten for its meat.

tcm.note: A classical tonic bird; warmer and more building than ordinary chicken.

histamine.note: Fresh poultry; the long simmer is what raises the soup.

nutrition.highlight: for the broth, not the meat

name: Chinese salted fish
description: Fish heavily salted and sun-dried — pungent enough that a small piece flavours a whole dish.

tcm.note: Salted and dried fish.

histamine.note: Salted and sun-dried fish — as high as this dataset goes.

name: Awarma
description: Lamb cooked down in its own fat and sealed under it — how meat was kept before refrigeration.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; preserved fatty meat.

histamine.note: Meat preserved for months under fat.

nutrition.highlight: how meat was kept, before fridges

name: Prosciutto
description: Pork leg salted and air-dried for a year or more, sliced thin enough to see through.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; salt-cured dried meat.

histamine.note: A year or more of curing — one of the highest-histamine foods there is.

nutrition.highlight: sliced until you can read through it

name: Mortadella
description: A large smooth pork sausage studded with fat cubes and scented with myrtle.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; a cooked cured sausage.

histamine.note: Cured and emulsified pork.

nutrition.highlight: the fat cubes are the point

name: Nduja
description: A soft fermented pork salami so heavy with chilli it spreads like paste.

tcm.note: Fermented cured pork with chilli.

histamine.note: A fermented salami plus a great deal of chilli.

nutrition.highlight: it spreads, which is unusual for salami

name: Bresaola
description: Beef salted with juniper and air-dried until deep red and lean.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; air-dried cured beef.

histamine.note: Air-dried cured meat.

name: Jamón ibérico
description: Acorn-fed black pig cured for three years or more — the fat melts at hand temperature.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; long-cured dried pork.

histamine.note: Three years of curing.

nutrition.highlight: the fat melts in your hand
